newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Sievert-fears of EMU turbulence overdone.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Sievert-fears of EMU turbulence overdone.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Olaf Sievert said on Tuesday that fears that financial markets will be very turbulent in the run-up to the start of European monetary union might be exaggerated.

In a speech at a reception in the eastern German city of Leipzig, where his regional central bank is based, Sievert said there was no reason for euphoria about EMU yet as countries would face two hard years before its start.
But he added that he did not expect market turbulence to contribute notably to the problems of those two years.

"I am not thinking here so much of the widespread fear that speculative trends on financial markets could create turbulence which will make the task of monetary policy more difficult," Sievert said according to the text of a speech released in advance of delivery.
"There are possibbly exaggerated worries here," he added.
He said growing consensus in financial markets that EMU would start on time in 1999 meant that any speculation was more likely to "stabilising speculation, and not destabilising speculation".
"That is in any case true for the internal relationship between the currency areas which will form a single currency area from the start of monetary union," Sievert added.
He added that it would be more difficult to ensure stable relationships between currencies which entered EMU and those initially left outside.

"It must also be acknowledged that the uncertainty as to who will be in from the start was rather increased, as even those countries which will not manage to reach the goal of meeting the entry criteria are making enormous efforts to do so," Sievert said.
Countries which wish to meld their currencies in the euro from 1999 onward must meet goals on public deficits, public debt, interest rates, exchange rates and inflation this year.
